values: Five-day vertical slice first. The live battle server owns turn state; Solana owns escrow and settlement.

Prototype rule: each five-second turn collects one hidden action from each player, then the authoritative server validates and resolves both actions from the same pre-turn snapshot. Wallet signatures remain outside the turn loop.
Approve Strike, Guard, and Recharge rules
The three actions, mana costs, simultaneous resolution, double KO, and invalid-action behavior match the Combat Rules sheet.
Damage, temporary guard, mana, 30-turn cap, timeout loss, and draw rules have shared constants and rules_version=2.
A typed contract covers players, ordered teams, active slots, HP, mana, turn number, deadline, hidden choices, events, and result.
Separate live play from Solana settlement
The server owns five-second turns. Solana owns teams, stake escrow, resolver authorization, final result hash, payout, and refund escape hatch.
Current auto-battle tests and program ID are recorded. New work does not silently reuse rules_version=1 matches.
Given a pre-turn snapshot and two actions, one deterministic function returns mana changes, damage, KOs, next active slots, events, and match status.
Test the complete 3 by 3 action matrix
All nine action pairs, insufficient mana, both attackers acting before KO, double KO, bench advance, and final draw are covered.
Every active SpeciesConfig has legal stats. Automated matchups report win rate, median turns, guard use, recharge use, and draw rate.
A dedicated TypeScript room starts only with both players, accepts validated actions, owns the deadline, and broadcasts one shared state.
Each room seat maps to the correct wallet. Turn choices do not open a wallet prompt. Spectators cannot submit actions.
Implement hidden choice and five-second deadline
A player's choice is acknowledged privately but not revealed before both lock or the server deadline. A missing or invalid choice becomes Recharge.
Reloading restores the latest authoritative snapshot. Three consecutive missed turns forfeit. A reconnect never restarts or pauses a deadline.
Change Match from auto-resolve to Active
join_match records both teams and stake, changes status to Active, and no longer calculates or pays a winner immediately.
GameConfig stores one resolver authority. Only that signer can record winner, turn count, and final event-log hash for an Active match.
If no valid result is recorded before the fixed expiry, either player can trigger an equal stake refund. Resolved matches cannot be refunded.
Creating or joining a match navigates both players to the same canonical match URL and restores that URL after reload.
Opponent card and bench sit at the top, turn state in the middle, own card and bench above a sticky three-button action tray.
Strike, Guard, and Recharge are at least 48px high, show mana cost or gain, disable impossible actions, expose keyboard focus, and show the five-second countdown.
Both cards animate from the same event. HP and mana bars interpolate, Guard flashes, Recharge pulses, and KO cards turn gray without changing game timing.
Reduced-motion mode uses fades and bar changes only. Spectators see the same deadline and events but no action controls.
Connecting, waiting, choice locked, opponent locked, reconnecting, forfeited, draw, and settlement unavailable states each have one clear message.
Persist and hash the authoritative event log
The server stores the ordered input and result events, derives one canonical SHA-256 result hash, and never accepts a client-provided winner.
Record the resolved result on Solana
The resolver signs a resolve transaction containing the match address, winner, turn count, and final hash. The Match account becomes Resolved once.
Let the winner claim the pot
Only the recorded winner can sign the claim. A draw refunds both. The exact transaction appears in match history.
Two wallets see the same 10 consecutive turns, HP, mana, KOs, result, transaction state, and claim outcome after refresh and one reconnect.
Median match length is 12 to 24 turns, draw rate is below 10%, no action is selected above 65%, and no sample creature exceeds 65% win rate.
Update demo script and operating notes
The demo explains simultaneous choices, one wallet signature for claim, current central resolver trust, and how to recover or refund a stuck match.
Move room presence and recovery to shared infrastructure
A room can recover after one server process restarts and multiple nodes can find the same match without split-brain state.
Replace trusted resolver with stronger settlement
Choose and prototype mutual result signatures, commit-reveal, or a replay-verifiable onchain result without changing the UI contract.
Add skills only after action telemetry
No skill ships until base action pick rates, match length, disconnect rate, and dominant strategies meet the V1 targets.

values: Editable design assumptions are highlighted in light green. All resolution is deterministic and uses integer arithmetic.
Keeps current ordered-team collection and match setup.
Deal deterministic damage to the opposing active creature.
Both clients count down from one server deadline.
Create temporary block equal to Shield for this turn. Unused block expires.
Plays after resolution and never changes the deadline.
Restore mana up to 5. Does not heal HP or create Shield.
Allows two early Strikes but creates a Recharge decision.
One visible resource shared by every creature.
A vulnerable turn usually funds one Strike and one Guard.
Caps stalling and keeps a match near two to four minutes.
Reconnect is possible, but an absent player cannot stall forever.
Version 1 remains the existing automatic battle.
Both living cards act from the pre-turn snapshot. Double KO is valid.
Guard applies only to incoming damage this turn.
Recharge is exposed to full damage.
Both spend mana. Temporary block expires unused.
Guard is wasted; Recharge gains mana.
Recharge is exposed to full damage.
Recharge gains mana; Guard expires unused.
Both gain mana up to the cap.
1. Raw damage = MAX(1, FLOOR((Attack + FLOOR(Speed / 5)) × 100 / (100 + defender Defense))).
2. Guarded damage = MAX(0, raw damage - defender Shield). Guard does not persist and Recharge does not restore HP or Shield.
3. Action eligibility is captured at turn start. Both living active creatures complete their selected action before KO checks.
4. If both active creatures reach 0 HP, both teams advance to the next slot together. If both final creatures fall, the result is Draw.
5. A choice is private until both players lock or the five-second deadline expires. Invalid or missing input becomes Recharge.
6. At turn 30, compare remaining HP as a percentage of each team's starting HP, then total mana. Equal values produce Draw and refund.
7. No random numbers, critical hits, dodge, healing, swapping, items, upgrades, or skills exist in this slice.
